title: 零售药柜工作坊教义001
instruction:
你是 Hedda Stavropoulos，Lanternwood Components 的社区药剂师，Idris Desrosiers 要求你将一个资助的想法转化为 Gildenhall Practice 一线团队可以实际运行的东西。今年秋天，会员委员会资助了在 Lanternwood Components 社区活动室举行的四场周六会议，可容纳 20 名成员，每场会议时间为 45 分钟，总材料预算为 $1,200，并且没有现有的讲义或脚本。为药柜清理会议准备研讨会概念和主持人指南，该会议可在今年秋天举办四次，并在明年再次使用。观众是为房间提供便利的一线员工，而不是可以即兴做出每项安全决定的药剂师，因此完成的文件必须独立存在，不得向作者提出任何问题。将完成的文档放在工作目录的顶层，使用文件名`medicine_cabinet_cleanout_workshop_guide.docx`。将其控制在不超过六页的范围内，包括任何面向参与者的文本，并使其易于在桌上打印和使用。
请包括：1) 一份简明的概念陈述，解释目标受众、目的、界限以及成功的会议让成员能够做什么； 2) 限时四十五分钟的辅导员指南，包含现实的过渡、房间管理语言以及足够的提问空间； 3) 面向参与者的语言，明确成员可以自行处理什么以及需要私人对话或推荐的内容； 4）基本材料、人员配置假设、准备需求以及保持在$1,200计划预算范围内的合理方式，而无需弥补价格或承诺我们尚未资助的资源； 5) 明确处理会员携带的药品，包括身份不明、过期、损坏、受控、冷藏或其他敏感物品，以及物品必须离开团体活动的时间点； 6) 针对有人将已故配偶的芬太尼贴片袋倒在桌子上这一棘手案件的回应，同时保护尊严并避免公开临床或法律声明； 7）为四次会议和明年制定一个简短的可重复性和反馈计划，并提供一种记录参与和问题的方法，而无需收集不必要的健康信息；和8）研讨会中使用的“清理”的确切含义，因为成员和工作人员目前使用该短语来表示组织橱柜和处置药物
s。不要编写药房系统点击说明、临床治疗方案、个性化药物评论或每个医学课程的一般讲座。请勿以会议形式代替某人的处方医生、药剂师、紧急服务部门或当地处置机构，也不得暗示团体主持人可以仅仅因为某种药物看起来陈旧或不需要而授权其服用、停止、重复使用、转移或丢弃。该指南应该是冷静和可用的，具有混合读写能力，应该在出现个人标签或丧亲之痛时保护隐私，并且应该以明确的操作立场结束，而不是列出未解决的后续想法。明确使用上面指定的人员和组织，不要发明第二个程序、第二个可交付成果或团队未提供的一组本地策略代码。

---

将您完成的工作写入**当前工作目录的顶层**，使用以下文件名：
- `medicine_cabinet_cleanout_workshop_guide.docx` — 可打印的研讨会概念和辅导员指南，供一线员工安全、可重复地提供 45 分钟的药柜清理课程。 （必须是工作目录顶层的 DOCX。；包括面向参与者的文本不得超过六页。；必须可供一线协调员使用，无需询问作者问题。；必须解决群体边界、隐私、敏感药物、转介、材料、预算纪律、可重复性和反馈。；不得包括药房系统点击说明、个性化药物审查或不受支持的本地政策代码。）

除了这些文件名之外，不会收集任何内容。在其他地方或以任何其他名称编写的正确文件得分为零。

gold.description: 沿用南杨原题包实际文件与已有公开预览。
gold.note: DOCX 正文与表格单元格文字提取；不还原分页、字体与版式。
gold.text:
Medicine-Cabinet Clean-Out Workshop
Facilitator guide • Four Saturday sessions, fall • Lanternwood Components community room
Prepared by Hedda Stavropoulos, Community Pharmacist, for the Gildenhall Practice frontline team. 45 minutes • up to 20 members • print this guide and the participant panel on page 3.
Concept and operating boundary
This is a calm, practical group workshop for members with mixed experience and literacy who want a safer, easier-to-use home medicine storage space. It helps people make an organisation plan, recognise when an item needs private professional follow-up, and leave knowing the next safe question to ask. Use short sentences, show the printed prompts, invite—not require—participation, and never ask people to explain their health.
Purpose
What success looks like
Not this workshop
Reduce clutter and mix-ups by planning a simple cabinet sort at home.
A member can name a private place to sort, keep medicines with their own packaging, use the “pause and ask” rule, and identify a disposal/referral next step.
Not an individual medication review, treatment discussion, disposal event, or a place to decide what someone should take.

What “clean-out” means here
“Clean-out” has two meanings. One is cabinet organisation: making a calm inventory and setting up a safe storage space. The other is disposal: sending an item through the applicable authorised disposal channel. In this workshop, clean-out means a bounded organisation-and-decision-preparation activity. Members practise a paper sorting plan and learn when to seek a disposal channel; they do not dispose of medicines here. Organisation does not determine whether any medicine is clinically appropriate.
DOCTRINAL LIMIT.  This workshop is not a substitute for a prescriber, pharmacist, emergency service, or local disposal authority. A facilitator cannot authorize a medicine to be started, stopped, reused, transferred, or discarded because it appears old, unwanted, or familiar.
Core rules — say before any activity
Members may
Members need a private conversation / referral when
Use the paper plan; talk generally about storage; keep their own medicines in their possession and in packaging; choose a later time and private place to sort at home.
The question concerns their own medicine, dose, whether to stop/continue, sharing, identity, expiry, a damaged item, disposal route, or personal health situation.
Ask general process questions; pass at any time.
There are urgent symptoms, poisoning, overdose, or immediate danger: stop the workshop conversation and contact emergency or poison-support services as appropriate.

Never identify or judge a medicine solely from an unverified appearance, a label fragment, or a participant guess. Do not taste, take, open, crush, or otherwise use medicines as part of this activity.


Run of Show
45 minutes exactly • one facilitator • questions stay bounded
Time
Facilitator action and words
Room-management cue
0–5 min
Welcome and orient. “You may participate or simply listen; participation is voluntary. Please do not display personal labels, names, or health details to the group.” Read the core rules.
Point to the privacy/safety panel. Invite bags to stay closed and with their owners.
5–10 min
Define clean-out. Demonstrate the paper plan only: Keep storage area / Ask privately / Find authorised disposal guidance. “These headings help organise a question; they do not decide whether a medicine is right for you.”
Use blank cards or pictured household items—not participant medicines.
10–20 min
Cabinet set-up activity. Members mark their own plan: a private, dry storage place; a “pause and ask” spot; a reminder to keep packaging together.
Pairs may discuss the plan, not medicines. Circulate for process help only.
20–30 min
Sorting rehearsal. Read two general situations and ask, “Which heading fits: organise, ask privately, or find a disposal channel?” Reinforce the stop condition.
If a member produces an item, pause that interaction: keep it with its owner; move to the private path.
30–38 min
Bounded questions. “I can take general process questions for eight minutes. Personal questions go on the private list, not into the room conversation.”
One question at a time; use a visible 8-minute timer.
38–43 min
Private-path and disposal closeout. Repeat that disposal depends on the applicable disposal channel; the workshop is not the disposal authority.
Collect no medicines. Hand out referral prompt.
43–45 min
Close. Ask one anonymous usefulness/process check. State the final operating position on page 6.
Thank members; keep sign-in separate from feedback.

Exact transition language
When…
Say…
A personal story begins
“Thank you for trusting us. I want to protect your privacy, so let’s pause the details here. We can use the private path after the group, or you can contact your pharmacist/prescriber.”
A question needs more than a minute
“That deserves proper attention, and this group cannot safely answer it. I’m noting only the topic—not your medicine name—for the private path. Let’s return to the next step on the plan.”
Someone presses for an answer
“I hear that you want an answer now. I cannot make that decision from this room, and I do not want to guess. The safe next step is a private conversation with the appropriate professional or authorised service.”

STOP CONDITION.  Stop any group handling immediately if there is uncertainty, an unidentified or sensitive item, damage/leakage, a personal clinical question, pressure for a decision, or an item is placed on the table. Do not pass it around. Keep it with its owner; use the private/referral path.


Participant Panel — Take This Home
Plain-language handout / display at the table
BEFORE YOU COME
IN THE ROOM
AT HOME
Bring a question or your paper list—not a bag of medicines. If you bring a medicine by mistake, keep it closed, with you, and out of view.
You may join in or just listen. Do not put medicines on the table. Do not show labels. Do not read names or health details aloud.
Choose a private time and place. Keep each medicine in its own packaging. Use the plan to organise; do not use it to decide what to take or stop.

Three simple steps
1. Organise your space
2. Pause and ask
3. Find the right channel
Choose a dry, private place away from children, visitors, heat, and moisture. Keep medicines with their packaging.
If you are unsure what an item is, whether to use it, or whether it is damaged, expired, refrigerated, controlled, or personal to someone else: stop. Keep it secure and ask privately.
For disposal, ask an appropriate pharmacist or disposal authority about the applicable authorised channel. The workshop does not collect or dispose of medicines.

Words the facilitator can use
If you ask…
The facilitator will say…
“Should I stop or keep taking this?”
“I can’t advise on your individual medicine in this group. Please keep it as it is and speak privately with your pharmacist or prescriber. If there is immediate danger, seek emergency help.”
“Can I give this to someone else?”
“Please do not share or transfer it. I can’t authorise that. Keep it with its owner and use a private professional conversation for the next step.”
“Can I throw this away now?”
“Please don’t make a disposal decision from the workshop. Keep it secure and ask the applicable authorised disposal channel; methods vary by item and place.”

Privacy and urgent help
Personal medication labels, names, and health details should not be read aloud or recorded for group purposes. Photographs of labels or medicines are not needed for attendance or feedback. If there is poisoning, overdose, urgent symptoms, or immediate danger, leave the workshop pathway and contact emergency or poison-support services as appropriate.
REMEMBER.  The activity teaches safe handling and next steps. It does not give permission to act on a specific medicine. If in doubt: pause, keep it secure, and ask privately.


Item Handling and Escalation
The facilitator does not take custody of participant medicines
Default: do not invite medicines into the room. If one appears, do not inspect it, read its label aloud, pass it around, or place it in a communal disposal container. The owner keeps possession and packaging unless an authorised channel and process are already established. No such arrangement is assumed for this program.
If an item is…
Group action
Private/referral action
Unidentified, loose, or label partly missing
Keep out of the group activity. Do not guess identity from appearance, fragment, or memory.
Owner keeps it secure; refer for appropriate professional handling.
Expired or no longer wanted
Do not say it is safe to use or safe to discard because of date alone.
Refer to the applicable authorised disposal channel; it determines disposition.
Damaged, leaking, contaminated, or compromised
Do not handle as an ordinary item. Stop the activity around it; do not pass it around.
Isolate from ordinary handling without taking custody; seek appropriate professional/authorised advice.
Refrigerated or temperature-sensitive
Do not treat as a room-temperature sorting item or keep it on the table.
Return it to appropriate storage promptly; refer privately for item-specific guidance.
Controlled or otherwise sensitive
No group discussion of labels or ordinary binning. Stop public handling and protect privacy.
Keep secure with the owner and route to appropriate professional or authorised support.

Sensitive item appears unexpectedly: general response
1) Calmly pause: “Let’s stop here and keep this private.”  2) Ask the member, without touching the item, to return it to their bag/packaging and keep it secure.  3) Move the conversation away from the table—outside the group’s hearing if practicable.  4) State only the next process step: private pharmacist/prescriber discussion, authorised disposal support, or urgent services as appropriate. Do not declare what the item is, what it means legally, or what must happen from the table.
Difficult case: deceased spouse’s fentanyl patches
SAY THIS.  “I’m sorry for your loss. Please don’t handle these here. Let’s pause the group activity around this table and move to a private space. Keep the patches secure with you; I cannot make a clinical or legal conclusion here. We will help you identify the appropriate pharmacist or authorised disposal support for a private next step.”
Do not count, inspect, touch, or publicly discuss the patches. Do not shame the member, debate ownership, promise a disposal method, or make legal pronouncements. Resume the group only after the item and conversation are away from the table; record only a minimal process incident if needed (see page 6).


Set-Up, Materials, Staffing, and Budget
Design for one group of up to 20 — not 20 consultations
Room and staffing assumptions
One Gildenhall Practice frontline facilitator leads the room. A second staff member is desirable when available for sign-in, timekeeping, and directing a private path, but is not required to deliver the core session. Pharmacist support is needed for a requested private medicine question, item-specific uncertainty, sensitive-item follow-up, or review of recurring safety issues—not to stand at every table. Arrange five tables of four facing a wall display; leave a clear private exit/side area. Each member works only on paper at their own seat. No communal medicine table, collection box, or label camera.
Essential — do not omit
Optional enhancements — remove first if unavailable
20 printed participant panels; 20 cabinet-plan sheets; pens; blank general-scenario cards; timer; visible privacy/safety boundary poster; sign-in count sheet; anonymous two-question feedback slips; a private conversation location.
Table tents; large-print duplicate panels; reusable folder/envelope for each member’s paper plan; display easel; refreshments.

Budget discipline: ceiling $1,200
No prices, donated resources, disposal contractor, room charge, or staff cost has been supplied. Therefore do not assert unit prices or promise any resource. Before session 1, obtain quotes/approvals and record actual commitments in these capped envelopes; total approvals and actuals must never exceed $1,200.
Approval envelope
Cap
Use / decision rule
Printing and accessible formats
$300
Print core panels and plans first; use the approved rate only.
Facilitation materials / reusable display
$250
Buy only safety-boundary display and paper activity aids after printing is secured.
Room/support contingency
$350
Use only if approved for the community-room delivery need; otherwise hold.
Accessibility / replacement contingency
$300
Use for approved access needs or replenishment across four sessions.
TOTAL MAXIMUM
$1,200
No purchase or commitment beyond this ceiling; unused amounts remain uncommitted.

If funds or materials are unavailable, simplify in this order: refreshments/table tents, folders/easel, reusable scenario cards (read scenarios aloud), then print one shared display plus plain paper plans. Never remove the privacy/safety boundary, paper plan, timer, or private-referral path.
Preparation checklist — complete before each Saturday
Room & print
People & privacy
Escalation & custody
☐ Tables for five groups of four; side/private space ready. ☐ Participant panels, plans, boundary poster, timer, pens, feedback slips ready.
☐ Facilitator has the scripts; optional support role confirmed. ☐ Sign-in is a headcount or voluntary first-name-only tally; no labels/photos.
☐ Know how to contact appropriate pharmacist, prescriber, emergency, poison-support, and authorised disposal services. ☐ Confirm no participant medicines will be collected or stored by the program without an authorised arrangement.



Repeat, Learn, and Close Safely
Same core guide four times this fall; improve process, not clinical decisions
Four-session repeatability
Use the same definition, agenda, scripts, participant panel, and stop condition for every session. Ordinary general questions fit the eight-minute question block; personal questions go to the private path. Between sessions, the facilitator and Hedda Stavropoulos (or the designated Gildenhall Practice pharmacist reviewer) review timing, attendance count, anonymous usefulness feedback, process/safety issues, recurring general questions, and materials used. Do not turn repeated questions into group clinical advice.
Minimal record
What to record
What not to record
Participation
Session date; number attending; number of paper panels distributed.
Diagnoses, medicine names, labels, personal histories, photographs, or reasons for attendance.
Feedback — separate prompts
Usefulness: “Did the session help you plan a safer cabinet sort?” (yes / partly / no). Process: “Was the room private and clear? Any safety/process concern?”
Health information or a request to explain a personal medicine.
Incident / near miss
Date; general process category (e.g., item placed on table, privacy redirection); action taken; whether issue was referred; reviewer/owner.
Names, clinical details, item name, label, photo, bereavement details, or a clinical conclusion.

The frontline facilitator sends the minimal record to the Gildenhall Practice designated workshop lead for review with Hedda Stavropoulos as pharmacist reviewer when a safety issue requires it. Urgent events follow the immediate emergency/poison-support pathway rather than this record. For next year, carry forward the stable core and approved materials; revise wording, timing, room flow, and print quantities based on the four-session review. Retain no extra health information to make the program “more useful.”
Facilitator quick responses
Need
Use these words
Routine process question
“I can explain the workshop process. For a decision about your own medicine, let’s use the private path.”
Private conversation requested
“We can step aside after this segment. Please keep the item with you and do not show the label to the group.”
Urgent safety concern
“This needs urgent help, not a workshop answer. Please contact emergency or poison-support services as appropriate now.”
Disposal question
“Different items and places use different authorised disposal channels. This workshop is not the disposal authority; keep it secure and ask the appropriate channel.”

Final operating position
THE SESSION OPERATES AS EDUCATION, NOT AUTHORIZATION.  Gildenhall Practice will run this 45-minute Lanternwood Components workshop four times with paper-based organisation practice, firm privacy and no-custody rules, bounded general questions, and private referral for item-specific decisions. Members leave with a safer plan and a next step—not a group decision about a medicine.
Version 1.0 • Prepared for fall delivery and next-year reuse • Owner: Gildenhall Practice workshop lead • Clinical reviewer: Hedda Stavropoulos

criteria.description: 该指南将车间标识为药柜清理车间，并将其命名为 Lanternwood Components 或其社区房间设置。
criteria.grader_hint: 确认程序和设置可从文档中识别。

original.criterion: The guide identifies the workshop as a medicine-cabinet clean-out workshop and names Lanternwood Components or its community-room setting.
original.grader_hint: Confirm the program and setting are identifiable from the document.

criteria.description: 该指南将 Gildenhall Practice 称为一线受众或运营合作伙伴。
criteria.grader_hint: 在渲染的文档中搜索 Gildenhall Practice。

original.criterion: The guide names Gildenhall Practice as the frontline audience or operating partner.
original.grader_hint: Search the rendered document for Gildenhall Practice.

criteria.description: 这个概念陈述了一个特定的目的，而不仅仅是描述有关药物的讨论。
criteria.grader_hint: 判断读者是否能够判断会议旨在解决哪些参与者问题。

original.criterion: The concept states a specific purpose rather than merely describing a discussion about medicines.
original.grader_hint: Judge whether a reader can tell what participant problem the session is intended to address.

criteria.description: 目标参与者受众以可用的术语进行描述，包括混合经验或文化水平。
criteria.grader_hint: 仅当观众描述改变了会议的交付方式时才授予奖励。

original.criterion: The intended participant audience is described in usable terms, including mixed experience or literacy.
original.grader_hint: Award only if the audience description changes how the session is delivered.

criteria.description: 该指南说明了成功的参与者在课程结束时可以做什么。
criteria.grader_hint: 寻找可观察的、有限的参与者结果。

original.criterion: The guide states what a successful participant can do by the end of the session.
original.grader_hint: Look for observable, bounded participant outcomes.

criteria.description: 该指南将清理定义为不同于内阁组织和处置，并解释了车间使用的含义。
criteria.grader_hint: 必须明确区分这两个经常混淆的含义。

original.criterion: The guide defines clean-out as distinct from both cabinet organisation and disposal, and explains which meaning the workshop uses.
original.grader_hint: The two commonly confused meanings must be explicitly separated.

criteria.description: 定义的范围足够窄，适合 45 分钟的小组会议。
criteria.grader_hint: 不要奖励需要单独审查的理想定义。

original.criterion: The defined scope is narrow enough for a 45-minute group session.
original.grader_hint: Do not award for an aspirational definition that would require individual reviews.

criteria.description: 该指南称，该研讨会不能替代处方医生、药剂师、紧急服务人员或处置机构。
criteria.grader_hint: 所有四个排除的替代品都应存在或明确涵盖。

original.criterion: The guide says the workshop is not a substitute for a prescriber, pharmacist, emergency service, or disposal authority.
original.grader_hint: All four excluded substitutes should be present or clearly covered.

criteria.description: 该指南指出，辅导员不能仅根据外观或年龄来授权启动、停止、重复使用、转移或丢弃药物。
criteria.grader_hint: 检查每个禁止的授权概念，允许等效的简单语言。

original.criterion: The guide states that a facilitator cannot authorize starting, stopping, reusing, transferring, or discarding a medicine based only on appearance or age.
original.grader_hint: Check each prohibited authorization concept, allowing equivalent plain language.

criteria.description: 该文件在最后给出了一个明确的操作立场，而不是以尚未解决的替代方案结束。
criteria.grader_hint: 结论应说明会议将如何运作，而不仅仅是提出未来的工作。

original.criterion: The document gives one clear operating position at its end rather than ending with unresolved alternatives.
original.grader_hint: The conclusion should state how the session will operate, not merely propose future work.

criteria.description: 渲染的 DOCX 不超过六页。
criteria.grader_hint: 渲染离线并计数页面，包括所有面向参与者的材料。

original.criterion: The rendered DOCX is no more than six pages.
original.grader_hint: Render offline and count pages including all participant-facing material.

criteria.description: 提交的文件是具有所需文件名的可读 DOCX。
criteria.grader_hint: 验证扩展名、可打开性和文件名；不要对这里的内容进行奖励。

original.criterion: The submitted file is a readable DOCX with the required filename.
original.grader_hint: Verify extension, openability, and filename; do not award for content here.

criteria.description: 一线员工可以使用该指南，而无需依赖作者未公开的知识。
criteria.grader_hint: 为所述受众判断操作的完整性和清晰度。

original.criterion: The guide is usable by a frontline employee without relying on the author’s unstated knowledge.
original.grader_hint: Judge operational completeness and clarity for the stated audience.

criteria.description: 定时议程总计 45 分钟，其活动符合既定的小组目标。
criteria.grader_hint: 将每个规定的持续时间相加并与45分钟进行比较；评估序列是否连贯。

original.criterion: The timed agenda sums to 45 minutes and its activities fit the stated group purpose.
original.grader_hint: Add every stated duration and compare with 45 minutes; assess whether the sequence is coherent.

criteria.description: 议程包括实践活动前的开场介绍和边界设定。
criteria.grader_hint: 边界必须在成员处理物品之前发生。

original.criterion: The agenda includes an opening orientation and boundary-setting moment before hands-on activity.
original.grader_hint: The boundary must occur before members handle items.

criteria.description: 议程包括实际的内阁组织或排序活动。
criteria.grader_hint: 仅靠讲座并不能满足这一标准。

original.criterion: The agenda includes a practical cabinet-organisation or sorting activity.
original.grader_hint: A lecture alone does not satisfy this criterion.

criteria.description: 该议程包括重申安全处置和转介界限的收尾。
criteria.grader_hint: 寻找有意识的结束活动，而不是突然停止活动。

original.criterion: The agenda includes a closeout that reiterates safe disposition and referral boundaries.
original.grader_hint: Look for a deliberate closing, not an abrupt stop at the activity.

criteria.description: 议程分配了一种现实的方式来处理问题，而不使会议成为开放式磋商。
criteria.grader_hint: 记下有限制的提问时间、停车场方法或类似方法。

original.criterion: The agenda allocates a realistic way to handle questions without making the session an open-ended consultation.
original.grader_hint: Credit a bounded question period, parking-lot approach, or equivalent.

criteria.description: 该指南提供了一个开场白，解释参与是自愿的，成员不应向团体展示个人标签。
criteria.grader_hint: 自愿参与和隐私指导都必须出现。

original.criterion: The guide supplies an opening script that explains participation is voluntary and members should not display personal labels to the group.
original.grader_hint: Both voluntary participation and privacy direction must appear.

criteria.description: 该指南告诉参与者将药品保留在自己的手中或包装中，除非指南明确指示安全、有限制的处理活动。
criteria.grader_hint: 寻找一个明确的默认值来防止不加区别的表转储。

original.criterion: The guide tells participants to keep medicines in their possession or packaging unless the guide expressly directs a safe, bounded handling activity.
original.grader_hint: Look for a clear default against indiscriminate table dumping.

criteria.description: 辅导员的指导使用适合混合读写能力的简单、非评判性语言。
criteria.grader_hint: 判断句子的复杂性、行话控制和语气。

original.criterion: The facilitator guidance uses plain, nonjudgmental language suitable for mixed literacy.
original.grader_hint: Judge sentence complexity, jargon control, and tone.

criteria.description: 该指南为参与者特定的问题提供了私人对话或转介路径。
criteria.grader_hint: 该路径必须识别协调员所说或所做的事情，而不仅仅是说“寻求帮助”。

original.criterion: The guide provides a private-conversation or referral path for a participant-specific question.
original.grader_hint: The path must identify what the facilitator says or does, not merely say ‘get help’.

criteria.description: 该指南将紧急症状、中毒、服药过量或直接危险从车间引导至适当的紧急或毒物支持服务。
criteria.grader_hint: 在没有发明本地电话号码的情况下，相信明显的直接危险升级。

original.criterion: The guide directs urgent symptoms, poisoning, overdose, or immediate danger away from the workshop to emergency or poison-support services as appropriate.
original.grader_hint: Credit a clear immediate-danger escalation without inventing a local phone number.

criteria.description: 该指南将常规信息需求与紧急安全问题区分开来。
criteria.grader_hint: 这种区别必须对协调员来说是可行的。

original.criterion: The guide distinguishes routine information needs from urgent safety concerns.
original.grader_hint: The distinction must be actionable for the facilitator.

criteria.description: 该指南表示，不要仅根据未经验证的外观、标签片段或参与者的猜测来识别或判断药物。
criteria.grader_hint: 寻找明确的验证限制。

original.criterion: The guide says not to identify or judge a medicine solely from an unverified appearance, label fragment, or participant guess.
original.grader_hint: Look for an explicit verification limit.

criteria.description: 不明药物不得参与团体活动，并转介进行适当的专业处理。
criteria.grader_hint: 排除和转介都必须注明。

original.criterion: Unidentified medicines are kept out of the group activity and referred for appropriate professional handling.
original.grader_hint: The exclusion and referral must both be stated.

criteria.description: 过期药物不会自动被协调员宣布可以安全使用或安全丢弃。
criteria.grader_hint: 该指南必须避免常见的关于过期的过分夸大。

original.criterion: Expired medicines are not automatically declared safe to use or safe to discard by the facilitator.
original.grader_hint: The guide must avoid the common overclaim about expiry.

criteria.description: 损坏、泄漏、污染或损坏的包装与普通处理隔离。
criteria.grader_hint: 任何明确的隔离和升级指令都符合资格。

original.criterion: Damaged, leaking, contaminated, or compromised packages are isolated from ordinary handling.
original.grader_hint: Any clear isolation and escalation instruction qualifies.

criteria.description: 冷藏或对温度敏感的药品不按普通常温分拣物品处理。
criteria.grader_hint: 寻找特定的温度敏感度边界。

original.criterion: Refrigerated or temperature-sensitive medicines are not treated as ordinary room-temperature sorting items.
original.grader_hint: Look for a specific temperature-sensitivity boundary.

criteria.description: 受管制药物需接受单独、谨慎的处理和转诊指导。
criteria.grader_hint: 该指南不得暗示普通分箱或小组讨论是合适的。

original.criterion: Controlled medicines receive a separate, cautious handling and referral instruction.
original.grader_hint: The guide must not imply ordinary binning or group discussion is appropriate.

criteria.description: 该指南指出，药品处置取决于适用的处置渠道，而不是普遍的家庭规则。
criteria.grader_hint: 仅当文件避免将一种不合格的处置方法呈现为普遍正确的情况下才予以认可。

original.criterion: The guide states that medicine disposal depends on the applicable disposal channel rather than a universal household rule.
original.grader_hint: Credit only if the document avoids presenting one unqualified disposal method as universally correct.

criteria.description: 主持人被告知不要在研讨会期间将参与者的药物放入公共处置容器中，除非已经建立了授权的渠道和流程。
criteria.grader_hint: 寻找针对临时收集的保护措施。

original.criterion: The facilitator is told not to place participant medicines into a communal disposal container during the workshop unless an authorised channel and process are already established.
original.grader_hint: Look for a protection against improvised collection.

criteria.description: 该指南解释了当敏感项目意外出现在桌子上时协调员会做什么。
criteria.grader_hint: 回应应涵盖暂停、隐私、安全分离和实际转介。

original.criterion: The guide explains what the facilitator does when a sensitive item appears unexpectedly on the table.
original.grader_hint: The response should cover pause, privacy, safe separation, and referral in practical terms.

criteria.description: 芬太尼贴片的丧亲场景得到了明确的解决。
criteria.grader_hint: 搜索芬太尼贴剂或明显等效的场景。

original.criterion: The fentanyl-patch bereavement scenario is addressed explicitly.
original.grader_hint: Search for fentanyl patches or an unmistakably equivalent scenario.

criteria.description: 在芬太尼场景中，协调员停止公共处理，并将对话和项目管理从小组中移开。
criteria.grader_hint: 停止公共活动和隐私都是必需的。

original.criterion: In the fentanyl scenario, the facilitator stops public handling and moves the conversation and item management away from the group.
original.grader_hint: Both public-activity cessation and privacy are required.

criteria.description: 在芬太尼场景中，指南避免宣布表格中的法律或临床结论，并将问题转交给适当的专业或授权支持。
criteria.grader_hint: 信用明确约束加上推荐，而不是单独推荐。

original.criterion: In the fentanyl scenario, the guide avoids declaring a legal or clinical conclusion from the table and routes the matter to appropriate professional or authorised support.
original.grader_hint: Credit explicit restraint plus referral, not referral alone.

criteria.description: 丧亲之痛的反应是富有同情心的，避免羞辱参与者。
criteria.grader_hint: 评估语气以及操作内容。

original.criterion: The bereavement response is compassionate and avoids shaming the participant.
original.grader_hint: Assess tone as well as operational content.

criteria.description: 该指南称，不应出于集体目的大声朗读或记录个人药物标签、姓名和健康详细信息。
criteria.grader_hint: 该文件必须解决公开披露和不必要的记录问题。

original.criterion: The guide says personal medication labels, names, and health details should not be read aloud or recorded for group purposes.
original.grader_hint: The document must address both public disclosure and unnecessary recording.

criteria.description: 该指南提供了一种尊重的方式来暂停或重定向正在披露敏感信息的参与者。
criteria.grader_hint: 寻找可用的词语或清晰的对话方式。

original.criterion: The guide provides a respectful way to pause or redirect a participant who is disclosing sensitive information.
original.grader_hint: Look for usable words or a clear conversational approach.

criteria.description: 该指南指出，出勤或反馈记录不应包含不必要的诊断、药物名称或个人病史。
criteria.grader_hint: 归功于显式数据最小化。

original.criterion: The guide states that attendance or feedback records should not contain unnecessary diagnoses, medicine names, or personal histories.
original.grader_hint: Credit explicit data minimisation.

criteria.description: 该指南描述了一种安全的物理设置，限制其他成员的药品和标签的使用。
criteria.grader_hint: 评估该设置是否适用于 20 名参与者。

original.criterion: The guide describes a safe physical setup that limits access to other members’ medicines and labels.
original.grader_hint: Assess whether the setup would work for twenty participants.

criteria.description: 该指南指定了明确的促进者角色，并确定何时需要药剂师支持。
criteria.grader_hint: 角色边界必须是可操作的，而不仅仅是人员配置。

original.criterion: The guide assigns a clear facilitator role and identifies when pharmacist support is needed.
original.grader_hint: The role boundary must be operational, not just a staffing count.

criteria.description: 房间规划和活动设计对于最多二十名成员来说是合理的，而不需要二十人同时进行咨询。
criteria.grader_hint: 一起判断容量、流量和个人注意力假设。

original.criterion: The room plan and activity design are plausible for up to twenty members without requiring twenty simultaneous consultations.
original.grader_hint: Judge capacity, flow, and individual-attention assumptions together.

criteria.description: 该指南为主持人提供了一种方法，可以避免某个参与者的问题占用小组会议的时间。
criteria.grader_hint: 信任保留尊严和时间的边界。

original.criterion: The guide gives the facilitator a method to keep one participant’s question from consuming the group session.
original.grader_hint: Credit a boundary that preserves dignity and time.

criteria.description: 材料清单包括参与者书写或分类辅助工具以及显示或分发指南安全边界的方法。
criteria.grader_hint: 寻找功能性材料，而不是不明原因的购物清单。

original.criterion: The materials list includes participant writing or sorting aids and a way to display or distribute the guide’s safety boundaries.
original.grader_hint: Look for functional materials, not an unexplained shopping list.

criteria.description: 该指南将基本材料与可选增强材料区分开来。
criteria.grader_hint: 这是使预算计划具有可操作性所必需的。

original.criterion: The guide distinguishes essential materials from optional enhancements.
original.grader_hint: This is needed to make the budget plan actionable.

criteria.description: 预算方法保持在$1,200上限内，无需断言不受支持的单价或承诺的资源。
criteria.grader_hint: 检查所有估计值是否都标记为假设，并且规定的总数不得超过上限。

original.criterion: The budget approach stays within the $1,200 ceiling without asserting unsupported unit prices or committed resources.
original.grader_hint: Check that any estimates are labelled assumptions and the stated total cannot exceed the ceiling.

criteria.description: 该指南确定了如果材料或资金不可用，首先要删除或简化的内容。
criteria.grader_hint: 相信优先的后备措施，而不是模糊的减少支出的指示。

original.criterion: The guide identifies what would be removed or simplified first if materials or funds are unavailable.
original.grader_hint: Credit a prioritised fallback, not a vague instruction to spend less.

criteria.description: 准备清单涵盖房间准备情况、印刷材料、人员配备、隐私和升级准备情况。
criteria.grader_hint: 应代表所有五个准备领域。

original.criterion: The preparation checklist covers room readiness, printed materials, staffing, privacy, and escalation readiness.
original.grader_hint: All five preparation domains should be represented.

criteria.description: 该指南包括会前检查，以确保未经授权安排，该计划不会收集或储存参与者的药物。
criteria.grader_hint: 寻找预防意外监护的方法。

original.criterion: The guide includes a pre-session check that no participant medicines are collected or stored by the program without an authorised arrangement.
original.grader_hint: Look for prevention of accidental custody.

criteria.description: 该指南包括主持人询问参与者是否停止或继续用药的措辞。
criteria.grader_hint: 措辞必须重新引导个性化决定，但又不至于听起来不屑一顾。

original.criterion: The guide includes facilitator wording for a participant asking whether to stop or continue a medicine.
original.grader_hint: The wording must redirect individualized decisions without sounding dismissive.

criteria.description: 该指南包括主持人的措辞，供参与者询问是否可以将某件物品送给另一个人。
criteria.grader_hint: 答案绝不能使药品共享正常化。

original.criterion: The guide includes facilitator wording for a participant asking whether an item can be given to another person.
original.grader_hint: The answer must not normalise medicine sharing.

criteria.description: 该指南包括主持人针对想要立即扔掉物品的参与者的措辞。
criteria.grader_hint: 评估应对措施是否避免了不安全的处置建议和不必要的警报。

original.criterion: The guide includes facilitator wording for a participant who wants to throw an item away immediately.
original.grader_hint: Assess whether the response avoids both unsafe disposal advice and needless alarm.

criteria.description: 该指南指出，参与者不应在活动中品尝、服用、打开、压碎或以其他方式使用药物。
criteria.grader_hint: 相信涵盖活动本身的明确的无用途规则。

original.criterion: The guide states that participants should not taste, take, open, crush, or otherwise use medicines as part of the activity.
original.grader_hint: Credit a clear no-use rule covering the activity itself.

criteria.description: 该指南避免对药物做出诊断、功效或治疗方面的声明。
criteria.grader_hint: 审查教义限制的主张，而不仅仅是免责声明。

original.criterion: The guide avoids making diagnosis, efficacy, or treatment claims about medicines.
original.grader_hint: Review claims for doctrinal restraint, not merely the disclaimer.

criteria.description: 该指南将其一般分类或组织规则与明确的声明配对，即该规则并不能确定药物是否适合临床。
criteria.grader_hint: 这是必需的规则/非声明配对。

original.criterion: The guide pairs its general sorting or organisation rule with an explicit statement that the rule does not determine whether a medicine is clinically appropriate.
original.grader_hint: This is the required rule/non-claim pairing.

criteria.description: 该指南将其处置转介规则与车间不是处置机构的明确声明配对。
criteria.grader_hint: 查找与规则相邻的限制。

original.criterion: The guide pairs its disposal referral rule with an explicit statement that the workshop is not the disposal authority.
original.grader_hint: Look for the limitation adjacent to the rule.

criteria.description: 该指南将安全处理教育与对特定药物采取行动的许可区分开来。
criteria.grader_hint: 这种区别在脚本和活动中应该保持一致。

original.criterion: The guide distinguishes education about safe handling from permission to act on a specific medicine.
original.grader_hint: This distinction should remain consistent across scripts and activities.

criteria.description: 该指南为任何团体处理活动确定了明确的停止条件。
criteria.grader_hint: 该情况应由不确定性、危险或个人临床需求触发。

original.criterion: The guide identifies a clear stop condition for any group handling activity.
original.grader_hint: The condition should be triggered by uncertainty, hazard, or personal clinical need.

criteria.description: 对于希望立即得到答案的参与者的分歧或压力，该指南给予协调员冷静的回应。
criteria.grader_hint: 评估措辞是否保护安全和融洽关系。

original.criterion: The guide gives the facilitator a calm response to disagreement or pressure from a participant who wants an immediate answer.
original.grader_hint: Assess whether the wording protects safety and rapport.

criteria.description: 该指南指出，团体出席或反馈不需要标签或药品的照片。
criteria.grader_hint: 归功于图像捕获的显式最小化。

original.criterion: The guide states that photographs of labels or medicines are not needed for group attendance or feedback.
original.grader_hint: Credit explicit minimisation of image capture.

criteria.description: 参与者的讲义或脚本使用混合读写能力的观众可以扫描的标题、标签或视觉结构。
criteria.grader_hint: 判断可浏览性，而不是装饰设计。

original.criterion: The participant handout or script uses headings, labels, or visual structure that a mixed-literacy audience can scan.
original.grader_hint: Judge scanability, not decorative design.

criteria.description: 该指南以减少个人药品在房间内暴露的方式告诉参与者该带或不带什么。
criteria.grader_hint: 该指令必须解决物理摄入边界。

original.criterion: The guide tells participants what to bring or not bring in a way that reduces exposure of personal medicines in the room.
original.grader_hint: The instruction must address the physical intake boundary.

criteria.description: 该活动可以重复四次，核心内容一致，同时允许提出普通问题。
criteria.grader_hint: 寻找一个稳定的引导者核心，而不是四个定制的活动。

original.criterion: The activity can be repeated four times with consistent core content while allowing ordinary questions.
original.grader_hint: Look for a stable facilitator core rather than four bespoke events.

criteria.description: 可重复性计划确定了会议之间应审查的内容。
criteria.grader_hint: 对事件、问题、时间安排或材料的信用审查。

original.criterion: The repeatability plan identifies what should be reviewed between sessions.
original.grader_hint: Credit review of incidents, questions, timing, or materials.

criteria.description: 可重复性计划确定了明年应结转或修订的内容。
criteria.grader_hint: 第四次会议之后，该计划不得停止。

original.criterion: The repeatability plan identifies what should be carried forward or revised for next year.
original.grader_hint: The plan must not stop after the fourth session.

criteria.description: 参与记录记录出勤情况，无需提供健康信息。
criteria.grader_hint: 检查建议的字段或类别以实现数据最小化。

original.criterion: The participation record captures attendance without requiring health information.
original.grader_hint: Check the proposed fields or categories for data minimisation.

criteria.description: 反馈方法分别捕获有用性和安全/过程问题。
criteria.grader_hint: 单一的满意度问题是不够的。

original.criterion: The feedback approach captures usefulness and safety/process issues separately.
original.grader_hint: A single satisfaction question is insufficient.

criteria.description: 该指南包括一种记录事件或未遂事故的方法，而无需记录不必要的个人临床细节。
criteria.grader_hint: 寻找最小的操作记录和升级路径。

original.criterion: The guide includes a way to record an incident or near miss without recording unnecessary personal clinical detail.
original.grader_hint: Look for a minimal operational record and escalation path.

criteria.description: 该文件明确了谁接收或审查研讨会问题和反馈。
criteria.grader_hint: 所有者可以是指定的角色而不是个人，但必须明确。

original.criterion: The document makes clear who receives or reviews workshop issues and feedback.
original.grader_hint: The owner may be a named role rather than a person, but must be clear.

criteria.description: 该指南不包括药房系统点击说明或临床治疗方案。
criteria.grader_hint: 检查文档中是否有排除的内容；当指南保持在范围内时奖励。

original.criterion: The guide does not include pharmacy-system click instructions or a clinical treatment protocol.
original.grader_hint: Inspect the document for excluded content; award when the guide stays within scope.

criteria.description: 该指南没有发明本地处置电话号码、政策代码或不受支持的法律要求。
criteria.grader_hint: 区分通用的推荐语言和捏造的当地事实。

original.criterion: The guide does not invent local disposal phone numbers, policy codes, or unsupported legal requirements.
original.grader_hint: Distinguish generic referral language from fabricated local facts.

criteria.description: 该文件对于会议是否处理组织、处置或两者都处理具有内部一致性。
criteria.grader_hint: 比较定义、议程、脚本和结论是否存在矛盾。

original.criterion: The document is internally consistent about whether the session handles organisation, disposal, or both.
original.grader_hint: Compare the definition, agenda, scripts, and conclusion for contradictions.

criteria.description: 该文件平静、尊重，适合与丧亲之痛相关的医学情况。
criteria.grader_hint: 一个技术上正确但冷漠或带有侮辱性的指南不应该接受这一点。

original.criterion: The document is calm, respectful, and suitable for a bereavement-related medicine situation.
original.grader_hint: A technically correct but cold or stigmatizing guide should not receive this point.

criteria.description: 最终指南平衡了参与者的有用性和禁止个体化临床决策。
criteria.grader_hint: 判断边界是否留下了一个可行的研讨会，而不是拒绝提供帮助。

original.criterion: The final guide balances participant usefulness with the prohibition on individualized clinical decisions.
original.grader_hint: Judge whether the boundaries leave a workable workshop rather than a refusal to help.

review.selection: 沿用旧review-500中南杨c0–c3固定随机100题，未重抽、未挑题。

validation_record.label: 结构/材料验收记录
validation_record.detail: validated 属于结构、防泄漏、材料推进验收；没有内容正确率结论。

author_policy_self_report_not_verified.reviewer_policy: Have an independent pharmacist or experienced medication-safety reviewer inspect the rendered DOCX against every rubric item, then independently verify page count, agenda arithmetic, budget ceiling, internal consistency, privacy minimisation, and absence of fabricated local policy details.
known_limitations: No jurisdiction-specific disposal authority or phone number is supplied, so the gold must use generic referral language rather than local legal instructions.
Exact visual layout may vary by office renderer; page count is assessed from the rendered submitted DOCX.

not_claimed: 不是本轮agent独立内容复审通过
不是正式正确率或RewardKit验收
不是证明此批质量排名第一

known_limitations: No jurisdiction-specific disposal authority or phone number is supplied, so the gold must use generic referral language rather than local legal instructions.
Exact visual layout may vary by office renderer; page count is assessed from the rendered submitted DOCX.

spec.professional_context: This is a retail-pharmacy communication artifact for a community workshop. The author must translate pharmacist judgment into safe, plain-language guidance that a non-pharmacist frontline facilitator can use without turning a group activity into individualized clinical care.
difficulty_sources: Translating pharmacist safety judgment into a self-contained guide for a non-pharmacist frontline facilitator
Resolving the tension between hands-on member participation and privacy/safe handling of sensitive medicines
Defining the ambiguous term clean-out before using it operationally
Pairing every safety rule with a clear statement of what it does not authorise
Keeping a realistic 45-minute, twenty-person workshop within a six-page and $1,200 constraint

authoring_plan.purpose: Build a six-page-or-shorter DOCX concept and facilitator guide from occupational knowledge for a 45-minute medicine-cabinet workshop delivered to up to twenty members by a frontline employee.
content_constraints: Use doctrinal mode: every material safety rule must be paired with a limitation on what it does not authorise.
Define clean-out as a bounded workshop concept and distinguish organisation from disposal.
Include an agenda totalling exactly 45 minutes with opening, boundary setting, practical activity, bounded questions, and closeout.

original_instruction:
You are Hedda Stavropoulos, the community pharmacist at Lanternwood Components, and Idris Desrosiers has asked you to turn a funded idea into something the Gildenhall Practice frontline team can actually run. The membership committee has funded four Saturday sessions in Lanternwood Components’ community room this fall, with space for twenty members, forty-five minutes per session, a total materials budget of $1,200, and no existing handout or script. Prepare a workshop concept and facilitator guide for a medicine-cabinet clean-out session that can be delivered four times this fall and used again next year. The audience is the frontline employee who will facilitate the room, not a pharmacist who can improvise every safety decision, so the finished document must stand on its own without a question to the author. Put the completed document in the top level of the working directory, using exactly the filename `medicine_cabinet_cleanout_workshop_guide.docx`. Keep it to no more than six pages, including any participant-facing text, and make it practical to print and use at the table. Please include: 1) a concise concept statement that explains the intended audience, purpose, boundaries, and what a successful session leaves members able to do; 2) a timed forty-five-minute facilitator guide with realistic transitions, room-management language, and enough breathing room for questions; 3) participant-facing language that makes clear what members may handle themselves and what requires a private conversation or referral; 4) the basic materials, staffing assumptions, preparation needs, and a defensible way to stay within the $1,200 program budget without making up prices or promising resources we have not funded; 5) a clear treatment of medicines brought by members, including unidentified, expired, damaged, controlled, refrigerated, or otherwise sensitive items, and the point at which an item must leave the group activity; 6) a response for the difficult case where someone empties a deceased spouse’s bag of fentanyl patches onto the table, while protecting dignity and avoiding public clinical or legal pronouncements; 7) a short repeatability and feedback plan for the four sessions and next year, with a way to record participation and issues without collecting unnecessary health information; and 8) the exact meaning of “clean-out” as used in the workshop, since members and staff currently use that phrase to mean both organizing a cabinet and disposing of medicines. Do not write pharmacy-system click instructions, a clinical treatment protocol, individualized medication reviews, or a general lecture on every medicine class. Do not present the session as a substitute for a person’s prescriber, pharmacist, emergency service, or local disposal authority, and do not imply that a group facilitator can authorize a medicine to be taken, stopped, reused, transferred, or discarded merely because it appears old or unwanted. The guide should be calm and usable with mixed literacy, should protect privacy when personal labels or bereavement arise, and should end with a clear operating position rather than a list of unresolved follow-up ideas. Use the named people and organisations above plainly, and do not invent a second program, a second deliverable, or a set of local policy codes that the team has not supplied.

---

Write your finished work to the **top level of the current working directory**, using exactly these filenames:

(Must be a DOCX in the top level of the working directory.; Must be no more than six pages including participant-facing text.; Must be usable by a frontline facilitator without asking the author a question.; Must address group boundaries, privacy, sensitive medicines, referrals, materials, budget discipline, repeatability, and feedback.; Must not include pharmacy-system click instructions, individualized medication reviews, or unsupported local policy codes.)
